title: GPU server purchase memo (one big vs two small)

items.text: Single point of failure: one box runs both training and the paying customer's live endpoint; any failure or maintenance takes everything down (with next-business-day repair)
match: if (it|the server|the machine|the box|that box) (fails|dies|breaks|goes down)
paraphrases: Single point of failure: if the one server dies, both training and Harrow's live endpoint go down.
No redundancy - with next-business-day repair, an outage could last days.
Two servers give failover for the customer endpoint; one box doesn't.

items.text: Utilization mismatch: 85% of jobs use 1-2 GPUs and only 3% use 8, so the interconnect advantage rarely matters while two boxes reduce queueing between users
paraphrases: The job log shows 85% of jobs use 1-2 GPUs; the 8-GPU fabric only helps the 3% quarterly fine-tune.
Two separate boxes cut queue contention for a team that already waits 3 hours for each other's jobs.
Optimizing for the rare 8-GPU job ignores the actual workload mix.

items.text: Lead time: the 8-GPU server takes 16 weeks to arrive, but the paying pilot starts in 6 weeks (4-GPU servers ship in 3)
paraphrases: Lead time: Option A arrives in 16 weeks but the Harrow pilot starts in 6.
The 4-GPU servers ship in 3 weeks; the 8-GPU box would miss the pilot deadline.
Delivery timing makes Option A unable to serve the customer in time.

items.text: Power: the 8-GPU server draws ~10.2 kW but the rack has only 6.5 kW free (8 kW limit minus 1.5 kW), so it needs a second rack too
paraphrases: Power: the 8-GPU server draws 10.2 kW but our rack only has 6.5 kW free - it won't fit.
It exceeds the 8 kW rack limit, so Option A also needs a second rack at $1.1k/month.
Rack power capacity rules out putting Option A in the existing rack.

items.text: The Harrow contract requires dedicated hardware not shared with any other workload; one shared box for training and Harrow violates it, whereas one of two servers can be dedicated
paraphrases: The Harrow contract requires dedicated hardware; running training on the same box would breach it.
Customer data must be isolated - with two servers one can be dedicated to Harrow.
Sharing one machine between internal training and Harrow's workload violates the pilot contract.

items.text: Rent the rare 8-GPU fine-tune in the cloud (~30 h x $98 = ~$3k per quarter) instead of buying for it
paraphrases: Rent an 8-GPU cloud instance for the quarterly fine-tune: 30 hours at $98/h is about $3k.
Burst to the cloud for the rare 8-GPU job instead of sizing the purchase around it.
On-demand rental covers the quarterly fine-tune for a fraction of the cost difference.

items.text: Resale value: 4-GPU servers keep ~55% after 2 years vs ~40% for 8-GPU systems with fewer buyers
paraphrases: Resale: 4-GPU servers keep about 55% of their value vs 40% for the 8-GPU box.
Two smaller servers are more liquid if we need to sell later.
Depreciation/residual value favors Option B.

items.text: Capital flexibility: with 14 months of runway and a board request to keep capex flexible, buying one 4-GPU server now and a second later is possible only with Option B
paraphrases: Board wants flexible capex with 14 months of runway: buy one 4-GPU server now and the second later.
Option B can be staged; Option A is an all-or-nothing $310k commitment.
Cash runway argues for a phased purchase.

decoys.text: Networking between two servers for distributed training was not considered
decoys.why_not: The memo includes 200 GbE NICs and switch in the $330k and measured the 1.6x multi-node slowdown.
paraphrases: Two servers need a fast network between them; the memo ignores interconnect costs.
Multi-node training needs 200 GbE switching, which isn't budgeted.
Bandwidth between nodes will bottleneck distributed training.

decoys.why_not: Both quotes include 3 years of next-business-day on-site support.
paraphrases: No warranty or vendor support plan is mentioned.
Hardware support contract should be compared.
Need a maintenance contract for the servers.

decoys.text: The memo doesn't compare buying with renting cloud capacity
decoys.why_not: The memo compares 24/7 rental at $41k/month and computes an ~8-month break-even.
paraphrases: The memo never compares buying hardware with renting cloud GPUs.
Cloud may be cheaper than owning - break-even analysis needed.
Leasing or hosted GPUs as an alternative to purchase are not evaluated.
